why: One pass over the n positions stores mismatch indices in lists ab/ba (up to n entries in total), then prints pairs from them in linear time.
Each of the n values does a bisect_right on the tails list h, which grows to n entries when the sequence is non-increasing.
The code's own k <= 40 guard limits the built string to about 21 characters, so neither work nor memory can grow with k.
At most four str.index scans of the input string, each O(n), and nothing else is stored (the input string itself is not counted as auxiliary).
One O(1) dict update per customer, and the dict can hold up to n distinct keys because the code does not bound h or m.
Reads the n points one at a time, keeping only four running min/max values.
Sorting a new n-element list costs O(n log n), but about n/2 list.pop(0) calls each shift the remaining list, which gives Theta(n^2) in total.

Trial division up to sqrt(N) of the value read. The divisor list KK and its reversed copy hold d(N) <= 2*sqrt(N) entries, and sorting and gcd over them cost less than the loop. Both bounds round up to O(n).
Two linear passes over the two input strings that print as they go; only counters are stored (the input strings are not counted).
Constant arithmetic for each of the t test cases, with nothing stored.
Sorting the n houses dominates; the edges and difference lists (about 2n entries each) are built in linear passes.
A sieve of Eratosthenes up to N costs n log log n, which rounds up to O(n log n); the boolean[N+1], the prime array and the HashSet take O(n) space.
n TreeSet insertions at O(log n) each plus a linear pass over the m girls; the TreeSet and its toArray copy hold up to n values.
For each of the n strings in A, a scan of B that breaks on a match gives O(n^2) comparisons of short tokens; the only storage is the input arrays, which are not counted.
The sieve marks multiples of every prime up to n+4 in n log log n time, which rounds up to O(n log n), using O(n) boolean and int arrays.
The n>36 guard caps the while loop at about 18 iterations, so the work is constant whatever value is read.
Constant arithmetic on three integers read from one line.
With n = length of the digit string read, the loop does n-1 Python string appends a+='9' (each copies O(n) per the conventions) and the stored strings are O(n) long.
Reads a string of length n and visits every k-th index for the read step k (worst case k=1 gives n iterations); the stored input string is the only O(n) memory.
Each of t test cases reads an n x m grid and builds and scans two n x m tables (rebound and freed between cases).
A fixed arithmetic comparison on three integers.
Each of t test cases reads n numbers into a list and does O(1) dict operations per element, then iterates the at most n dict keys.
Four str.count scans with constant-length patterns over the read string of length n; storing that input string is the only O(n) memory (the function itself uses O(1)).
Constant arithmetic on three integers.
If the value n has no lucky divisor (e.g. n prime) no early return fires, so the loop runs x = 2..n-1 with constant-cost checks against a fixed 14-element list; range is lazy.
A hand-written insertion sort over the n houses is quadratic on reverse-sorted input; two double arrays of size n are allocated.
Reads n integers into an int array and makes two linear passes to find the minimum and second minimum.
Fills an int array of 2n wall endpoints, sorts it with Arrays.sort, then scans it once.
Parses the n numbers on one line into an ArrayList, sorts it with Collections.sort and scans it linearly.
Builds an array of n rect objects, sorts it with Arrays.sort and does one linear pass over neighbours.
For each of t test cases it stores an n x m grid and does O(n*m) work counting dots per row, per column (zip transpose) and scanning every cell.
Builds a list of about n/2 '2' strings and joins them into an O(n)-length string, where n is the integer value read.
One O(1) dict update per input line with up to n distinct (a,b) keys stored, then a max over the values.
Each of n values does a bisect on a sorted tails list of size up to n; the input list, its slice copy and the tails list are O(n).
A fixed number of comparisons on three integers.
Builds the answer with e += char n times, each concatenation copying O(n) characters; the stored strings are O(n).
n points each update three hash maps in O(1), then each map of up to n keys is iterated once.
Loop j up to n/2 does an O(1) modulo per step (str(j) is built only for divisors via short-circuit and); only O(log n)-digit strings are allocated.
Counts the n values with a Counter and sorts up to n frequencies; the list, counter and sorted copy are O(n).
Stores the n input pairs in a list, then one linear pass finds the longest run of equal consecutive pairs.
Reads n numbers into an int[n] and makes three linear passes to find the minimum and the next larger value.
Up to n TreeMap insertions plus at most n left-pointer removals, each O(log n); int[n] plus a TreeMap of up to n keys.
Sorts the n houses with Collections.sort, then builds O(n)-size edge and difference lists in linear passes.
Sieve of Eratosthenes to n (marking from primes <= sqrt n) is n log log n, rounded up to the n log n class; boolean[n+1] and the primes list are O(n).
Exchange sort with nested i<j loops does n(n-1)/2 comparisons; two int[n] arrays are stored.
No loops: three fixed gesture words are compared via a 3-entry dict, so nothing grows with the input.
Each of t cases reads and stores an n x m grid and scans rows, columns and up to n*m max-row/max-col pairs (all-'*' grid); space counts the stored grid.
One linear DP pass; the input list and the dp array both hold n values.
Single loop over the n-character string; space is the stored input string (O(1) if stored input were not counted).
Constant number of comparisons on three integers.
After the O(n log n) sort, every other pop(0) shifts the remaining list, about n^2/4 moves in total; the list holds n values.
Enumerates all C(n,3) triples with O(1) work each; the sorted list and the combinations pool copy are O(n).
Enumerates all C(n,3) triples; the only growing allocation is the stored n-tuple of input (combinations reuses it as its pool).
Up to n (the value) O(1) iterations; check, costing O(log n) via str, runs only on the o(n) divisors, and its digit string is O(log n).
On 'ABAB...' every position copies the slice a[i+2:] and rfinds in it, O(n) each with no break; the slice and the input string are O(n).
The outer loop is a fixed 8001-value range (constant) around an n-iteration loop; space is the two int[n] input arrays.
Partial sums of 4^i pass k after about log4 k terms, so for valid k >= 1 both loops run O(min(n, log k)) times per test case (BigInteger ops taken as O(1)); bs holds that many values.
The hand-written exchange sort always does n(n-1)/2 comparisons; space is the two int[n] input arrays.
About pi(n) ~ n/log n calls to ArrayList.contains each scan up to pi(n) primes, dominating the sieve; boolean[n+1] array plus the prime list.
Arrays.sort of n objects then one linear pass; the array holds n objects.
Loops over the n input characters, then int(s) and ten mods on that n-digit number are O(n); s and int(s) use O(n) space (n = string length, not the integer's value).
Each of the t test cases builds and prints a list of n numbers, so O(n) work per case and an O(n) list at peak.
The while loop subtracts 2 from min(n, m) until it is at most 1, about min(n, m)/2 iterations, using only scalars.
Only reading and storing the length-n second line scales and printing n+1 is constant work, so it would be O(1)/O(1) if stdin reading and stored input were treated as free.
Reads one integer and performs a fixed set of 14 modulo checks.
Four str.count scans of the length-n input string are O(n), and the only O(n) storage is that read string itself (O(1) extra if stored input were not counted).
input() + 'X' builds a new length n+1 string and the loop does n constant-time adjacent comparisons.
Counter is O(n) but most_common() sorts up to n distinct (value, count) pairs, and the array, counter, sorted list, reversed copy and slice are all O(n).
One constant-time formula per test case with nothing kept across iterations.
Each of the t test cases may build and print a K-element list ([2]*K or [1]*K), so O(k) work and O(k) peak space per case.
Each of the t test cases may append k elements to a list and print it, giving O(k) work and O(k) peak space per case.
Reads n time pairs into the new list c and scans its adjacent gaps once, both linear.
Two array accesses and an addition regardless of the array length.
Single pass over n points keeping four running min/max scalars; the 'mines' list stays empty.
Recursion enumerates a fixed 27 three-char strings regardless of input, then n is tested against at most 27 constants.
Fixed 3x3x2 loops doing constant arithmetic on the one number read.
One pass over the n-char string; the stored input string is the only O(n) memory (O(1) if stored input were excluded).
One O(n) split plus scan per distinct char of s; k distinct chars can reach n with an unrestricted alphabet (O(n) if fixed to 26 letters); split lists are O(n).
Loop i=1..n calls str(i) three times at O(log i) each; li holds every 4/7-only number <= n, about n^0.301 of them, rounded up to O(n).
Four linear str.count passes; the stored input string is the only O(n) memory (O(1) if stored input were excluded).
Reads n integers into a new list and sorts it.
Each of t test cases prints up to b-1 values in a loop without storing them.
d = m/n is repeatedly divided by 2 then by 3, so both loops run O(log(m/n)) times.
Membership test plus at most 14 int()/mod operations against a fixed 14-element list on one read number (O(log n) only if digit parsing were charged).
In-place iterative heap sort: O(n) heapify plus n-1 O(log n) sift-downs; returns the input array.
Allocates, fills and returns an n x n matrix.
For each of the O(n^2) index pairs of the 2n-element array it builds an O(n) list without that pair and scans it in O(n).
Each of t test cases builds and prints a fresh length-n list.
Loops i over 1..n with an O(1) modulo; the O(log i) digit check runs only for divisors of n (at most 2*sqrt(n)), so O(n) total with O(1) memory.
Tests n against a fixed list of 14 lucky numbers, independent of n.
Two stack-based topological passes over n nodes with at most one out-edge each, using O(n) adjacency lists, degree arrays and answer list.
Only prints constants and len(s)*2-1 with nothing iterating over s; it becomes O(n) time and space only if reading and holding the input line is counted.
Slices the suffix arr[k-1:] and builds a set from it (O(n) time and space), then walks left at most k steps.
A fixed 3x2x2 loop over constant digit lists testing divisibility, independent of n.
Enumerates all C(n,3) triples with O(1) work each; combinations copies the n-element pool into a tuple, so O(n) space.
Reads three integers and makes a constant number of comparisons.
Loops i over 2..n with an O(1) modulo, building str(i) (O(log n) chars) only for divisors of n, so O(n) time and an O(log n) temporary string (O(1) if digit strings are ignored).
Iterative binary search halves [lo, hi] each step using a few int variables.
linearScan scans arr once with O(1) extra memory; main only calls it on a fixed 4-element array (the fixed driver run alone would be O(1)).
Sorts the n items, then fills an (n+1) x m DP table where m is the budget t read from input.
Two str.index scans plus a stride-k walk between G and T over the length-n string; only scalars beyond the read input (stored input not counted as auxiliary).
One pass over n character pairs, but each out += c copies the growing string (O(length) per convention) and out reaches length n.
Constant modulo checks, then str(t) and a scan over its ~log n digits.
Loops i = 1..n (the value read), digit-checking only divisors; with no lucky divisor (e.g. n prime) all n iterations run, using only scalars.
Each of t test cases may build and print a list of k elements (k <= n when built); one such list is alive at a time.
Membership test in a fixed 14-element list and at most 9 modulo checks; nothing grows with the input.
Single pass over the n-character string with two counters; the stored input string is not counted as auxiliary.
Appends n/2 strings to a list (n is the value read) and joins them into an O(n) output string.
Only work is reading the unused n-character command line and printing n+1 (O(1) if input reading is not charged); the stored line is input, not auxiliary.
Repeatedly divides x = m/n by 3 and then by 2, O(log m) iterations for m >= 1, with only scalars.
binarySearch halves [lo, hi] over an array of length n in O(1) space; main merely runs it on a fixed 4-element array (O(1) if the driver itself is the unit).
For each i, findIndexOfMin scans i+1..n-1 (about n^2/2 comparisons) and swaps in place, returning the same array.
